definitions.explanation: How a person was raised, and the manners and behavior that result from their upbringing. Often used to comment on whether someone shows signs of a good or poor upbringing.
The way something (a person, plant, or animal) has grown or developed. Often used in compounds with a place name to indicate where someone grew up.

examples.japanese: {育|そだ}ちの{良|よ}さが{感|かん}じられる。
examples.english: You can sense a good upbringing.

examples.japanese: {食|た}べ{方|かた}を{見|み}れば{育|そだ}ちが{分|わ}かると{言|い}われる。
examples.english: It's said that you can tell someone's upbringing from the way they eat.

examples.japanese: {生|う}まれは{大阪|おおさか}だが、{育|そだ}ちは{東京|とうきょう}だ。
examples.english: I was born in Osaka, but I grew up in Tokyo.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{東京|とうきょう}{育|そだ}ちなので{方言|ほうげん}を{話|はな}さない。
examples.english: She grew up in Tokyo, so she doesn't speak dialect.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}は{天候|てんこう}が{良|よ}かったおかげで、{野菜|やさい}の{育|そだ}ちがいい。
examples.english: Thanks to the good weather this year, the vegetables are growing well.

examples.japanese: {生|う}まれも{育|そだ}ちも{北海道|ほっかいどう}で、{子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}から{雪|ゆき}には{慣|な}れている。
examples.english: I was both born and raised in Hokkaido, so I've been used to snow since childhood.

notes:
USAGE NOTE:
The set phrase {生|う}まれも{育|そだ}ちも (both born and raised in) is extremely common in self-introductions. When commenting on upbringing quality, {育|そだ}ちが{良|い}い/{悪|わる}い is a common but potentially judgmental expression.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {育|そだ}ちが{良|い}い (well-bred, well-raised)
- {育|そだ}ちが{悪|わる}い (poorly raised)
- {東京|とうきょう}{育|そだ}ち (raised in Tokyo)
- {生|う}まれも{育|そだ}ちも (both born and raised in)
- {育|そだ}ちがいい (growing well — for plants)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {育|そだ}て: child-rearing, raising (active — the parent's perspective)
- {出身|しゅっしん}: origin, where one is from (more neutral/factual)
